description: Computational Cognitive Science is built on probability: conditional probability, Bayes' rule, expectations, the Beta and binomial distributions, and comfort with sums and integrals over hypothesis spaces. The source course (MIT 9.66J) requires 'a class in probability or statistics'; a measure-theoretic background more than suffices.
Labs and the final modelling project implement small Bayesian models in Python; the source course expected programming experience in a high-level language.

The course fits models by maximum likelihood and compares them by information criteria and held-out log-likelihood, so it asks for likelihood and basic model fitting. Measure-theoretic probability covers the mathematics, not the practice of fitting a model: demonstrated maximum-likelihood estimation meets the rule, or NEU-220, whose unit 2 teaches model fitting, serves as the bridge.

alternatives.label: Model fitting in NEU-220 (unit 2) as a bridge

description: Comfort with probability and with a model that makes predictions. Reinforcement-learning basics help but are introduced where they are needed.
